Metabolic pathways inferred from the Prokka annotations with MinPath. Commands for this step were run in `minpath/`.

# Step 8: Infer metabolic pathways
 
```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/minpath

head ../prokka/metabat.2/metabat.2.tsv

head ../prokka/metabat.2/metabat.2.tsv | awk -F '\t' '{print $1,$5}' #transform tsv to include unique ID

head ../prokka/metabat.2/metabat.2.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{print $1,$5}' #filter output to only include EC number

head ../prokka/metabat.2/metabat.2.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus' #remove header line

cat ../prokka/metabat.2/metabat.2.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus' #include all genes

```

Run minpath 
```{bash}
cat ../prokka/metabat.2/metabat.2.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus' > metabat.2.ec # input for minpath

minpath -ec metabat.2.ec -report metabat.2.ec.report -details metabat.2.ec.details 

head metabat.2.ec.report #output 
```

### PWY-7321 (XX) 
- which is a pathway identifier in the metacyc database. You can use this to lookup the full pathway. Eg PWY-7321
### naive 1 
- tells us that at least one gene from this pathway was found. Simply calling a pathway present whenever one of its genes is found is the “naive” approach (ignore*)
### minpath 1 
- tells us that minpath kept this pathway in its minimal set of pathways. If this says minpath 0 then minpath decided that the genes found are better explained by other pathways, so the evidence for this one is weak (0 - non neseccary to explain genes in organism, while it might still contain these genes)
### fam0 4 
- tells us that four gene families are involved in this pathway
### fam-found 2 
- tells us that we found 2 gene families from the pathway in this genome
### name ecdysteroid metabolism (arthropods) 
- is a name for the pathway

Prepare minpath for bins from prokka 
```{bash}
while read bin;do 
  cat ../prokka/$bin/${bin}.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{printf("%s\t%s\n", $1,$5)}' | grep -v '^locus' > ${bin}.ec 
done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```

Run minpath on every bin
```{bash}
while read bin;do 
  minpath -ec ${bin}.ec -report ${bin}.ec.report -details ${bin}.ec.details
done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```

## PWY-101 photosynthesis light reactions 
This pathway includes the essential components of photosynthesis that occur in light, Photosystem I and Photosystem II.
```{bash}
grep 'PWY-101' *.ec.report
```
Output: 
contig_116.ec.report:path PWY-101 any n/a  naive 1  minpath 0  fam0  4  fam-found  1  name  photosynthesis light reactions
metabat.2.ec.report:path PWY-101 any n/a  naive 1  minpath 1  fam0  4  fam-found  4  name  photosynthesis light reactions
metabat.33.ec.report:path PWY-101 any n/a  naive 1  minpath 0  fam0  4  fam-found  1  name  photosynthesis light reactions
metabat.71.ec.report:path PWY-101 any n/a  naive 1  minpath 1  fam0  4  fam-found  1  name  photosynthesis light reactions



# PWY-5360 superpathway of tetrathionate reduction
This pathway is important because it includes enzymes required to reduce sulfite to hydrogen sulfide. Note that sulfite acts as the terminal electron acceptor in this pathway, however, in a broader sense the term “sulfate reducing” refers to micro-organisms that can produce sulfide from a range of oxidised sulfur compounds.

```{bash}
grep 'PWY-5360' *.ec.report

```
Output:
metabat.6.ec.report:path PWY-5360 any n/a  naive 1  minpath 0  fam0  3  fam-found  1  name  superpathway of tetrathionate reduction (Salmonella typhimurium)

Question 4.2
How many bins contain the pathway PWY-5360?
- PWY-5360 = 1 bin (metabat6)

What order (in a taxonomic sense) do these bins belong to? Are they in the same family?
metabat.6
Based on minpath = (Salmonella typhimurium)
Based on gtdbk Bacteria: Camplyobacterota / Arobacteraceae / Halacrobacter
